Figures come from the Census Bureau and CMS (September 2026).

With roughly 68,317 residents age 65 and older, Lehigh County is 11th among 67 Pennsylvania counties for older residents. That group is 18.1% of its population, compared with 20.0% across Pennsylvania. The 24,149 residents now between 60 and 64 will become Medicare-eligible soon, and our turning 65 guide walks through it. By age, the 65-and-older group splits 58% ages 65 to 74, 31% ages 75 to 84 and 11% age 85 and up (Census 2023). CMS data show 47.3% of Lehigh County residents with Medicare chose Medicare Advantage, which is lower than the 54.5% average across Pennsylvania. A county average does not tell you which kind of plan fits you. Whether Medicare Advantage or Original Medicare with a Medigap plan is the better fit depends on your doctors, your prescriptions and how you want to handle costs, so we compare both for your ZIP code.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.
  • A list of your prescriptions and the pharmacy you use.
  • Whether you have Medicaid or get help paying Medicare costs.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Who has Medicare in Lehigh County

Lehigh County sits in a metro area, which the USDA defines as counties in metro areas of 250,000 to 1 million population. That usually means more doctors, more hospitals and more plan choices in the area.

CMS counts 82,128 Medicare beneficiaries in Lehigh County (2023). Their average age is 73, about the same as the Pennsylvania average of 73. About 12% are “dual eligible,” meaning they have both Medicare and Medicaid, close to the state figure of 14%.

Among people in Original Medicare in Lehigh County, CMS reported about 585 emergency room visits and 260 inpatient hospital stays per 1,000 beneficiaries in 2023, which is close to the state average for emergency visits (565) and close to it for hospital stays (239). About 7% received home health care. These figures describe how people use care under Original Medicare; they do not show what any plan covers or costs.

Sources: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation, 2023; USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, 2023.

Medicare Advantage and Part D plan availability and provider networks are set county by county, so the plans open to you in Lehigh County may differ from those in a neighboring county. We are not based in Lehigh County; we help Lehigh County residents by phone or video call.

Hospitals located in Lehigh County

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) lists these hospitals in Lehigh County:

  • Lehigh Valley Hospital — Allentown (acute care; nonprofit; emergency services; CMS overall rating 4 of 5)
  • Lehigh Valley Hospital - Macungie — Macungie (acute care; for-profit; emergency services)

Being located in the county is not the same as being in your plan’s network. Each Medicare Advantage plan builds its own network, so we confirm that your hospital and your doctors are included before you choose. Ratings are CMS Care Compare overall hospital star ratings; they describe the hospital, not whether a plan covers it. Source: CMS Hospital General Information.

Where people live in Lehigh County

The largest communities in Lehigh County by 2023 Census population estimates are Allentown (124,880), Bethlehem (19,951), Emmaus (12,017), Catasauqua (6,469), Fountain Hill (4,798), Slatington (4,250). Each figure counts only the people living inside the county.

We look up plans by ZIP code. In Lehigh County, that means areas such as 18018, 18031, 18032, 18034, 18036, 18037, 18046, 18049, 18051, 18052, 18053, 18059, 18062, 18065 and 14 more, based on Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that lie mostly in the county.

Common questions

Lehigh County Medicare FAQ

Can I get help with Medicare in Lehigh County by phone?
Yes. Phone and video appointments are how we serve Lehigh County. We hold a Pennsylvania license, compare plans from many carriers and walk you through them from home, with no pressure to enroll.
Will my Lehigh County doctors and hospitals be covered?
On a Medicare Advantage plan it depends on that plan’s network, so before you enroll we check whether your doctors and the hospitals you use, such as Lehigh Valley Hospital, Lehigh Valley Hospital - Macungie, are in network. With a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plan you can see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
How many people in Lehigh County have Medicare Advantage?
CMS reported 39,742 people enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan out of 84,013 people with Medicare in Lehigh County in September 2026, or 47.3%. The Pennsylvania average was 54.5%.
Do you charge Lehigh County residents for help?
No. You pay nothing to work with us. Carriers compensate us, and the price of your plan is the same as if you enrolled directly.
When can I enroll or change plans?
You can enroll during your Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period if you have a qualifying event such as moving into or within the county.
